info.description:
Machine-consumable HTTP surface of an ISCC Monitor instance: the tlog-tiles mirror artifacts, the computed RFC-6962 inclusion/consistency proofs, single-leaf record bytes, the downloadable proof bundle, the verify-for-me verdict, and the liveness/version/metrics endpoints.

This contract describes ONLY the machine surface (JSON, opaque-byte artifacts, and Prometheus text). The human-facing server-rendered HTML surfaces — the realm index (`/`), the hub dossier (`/{domain}`), the log browser, and the HTML Certificate of Inclusion (`/inclusion/{iscc_id}`) — are deliberately OUT of this contract; they are documented by their rendered HTML and CLAUDE.md, not by OpenAPI.

Every public GET answers cross-origin browser requests with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. The monitor is a verifiable cache, not a trusted oracle: prefer the client-verified proof bundle over the verify-for-me verdict (see that operation's description).
info.title: ISCC Monitor API

get.description: Reports process liveness and SQLite store readiness. A non-200 means the instance is not ready to serve.

200.description: The instance is live and the store is ready.

get.description: Returns a self-contained proof bundle — the hub-signed checkpoint, the inclusion proof, the record bytes, the hub key, and an OTS proof when anchored — that a client verifies on its own, removing the monitor from the trust path (the authoritative tier-2 path). The id is the self-describing ISCC-IDv1; the issuing hub is resolved realm-wide. The bundle is offered only when the monitor re-verified the inclusion proof against the accepted root; a non-certifiable id is an honest 200 "no proof bundle available", never a fabricated bundle and never a 5xx.

parameters.description: The self-describing ISCC-IDv1 (the `.bundle` suffix selects the machine artifact).
parameters.name: iscc_id

200.description: The proof bundle as a JSON attachment, OR an honest "no proof bundle available" verdict for a non-certifiable id.

get.description: Prometheus text exposition of the monitor's series — hub status, last-observed sizes, poll failures, and violations. This is the Prometheus text format, not a JSON document, so it carries no JSON response schema.
The in-repo OpenAPI document, served byte-verbatim as JSON.
The in-repo OpenAPI document, served byte-verbatim as YAML.
Returns the build-provenance string (the git short SHA, or the `dev` default for an un-stamped build), so an operator can confirm exactly which build is live.
Returns the hub-signed checkpoint note (the tlog-tiles `checkpoint` artifact) for the accepted `(size, root)`, served verbatim from the local mirror. Distinct from the `.ots` Bitcoin-anchor proof.

Returns the OpenTimestamps proof for the accepted `(size, root)`, served verbatim as an opaque byte stream so a client can run the standard `ots` toolchain against it. A different artifact from the signed `/checkpoint` note: this is the Bitcoin-anchor timestamp proof.

404.description: No accepted checkpoint yet, or the root is not yet anchored.

get.summary: Mirrored OpenTimestamps proof for the accepted root.

get.description: Returns the RFC-6962 consistency proof relating a client's prior trusted tree size (`from`) to the monitor's accepted tree size, computed from the local mirror. The degenerate `from == 0` and `from == accepted size` cases return an empty proof (200).

parameters.description: The client's prior trusted tree size (M ≤ N, the accepted size).
parameters.name: from

400.description: Missing or non-numeric `from`, or `from` exceeds the accepted size.

404.description: No accepted checkpoint yet, `from` has no recorded checkpoint, or a tile is not mirrored.

get.summary: Computed consistency proof to the accepted checkpoint.

get.description: Returns the raw bytes of exactly one accepted leaf, addressed by its absolute leaf sequence (`index`), decoded from the mirrored entry bundle. This is one leaf's bytes, distinct from the raw whole-bundle BLOB served under `/tile/entries/...`.

404.description: No accepted checkpoint yet, or the leaf is not covered by the accepted checkpoint.

get.summary: Single-leaf record bytes from the mirror.

get.description: Returns the RFC-6962 inclusion proof for the named ISCC-ID against the monitor's accepted checkpoint, computed entirely from the local mirror (never re-hitting the hub). The default leaf is the lowest committed sequence for the id; an explicit `index` selects a specific committed sequence. The response mirrors the hub's `IsccLogInclusionProof` shape.

parameters.description: The ISCC-ID to prove inclusion for (with or without the `ISCC:` prefix).
parameters.name: iscc_id

parameters.description: An explicit committed leaf sequence; must match a committed seq for the id.
parameters.name: index

404.description: The id is unknown, the leaf is not covered by the accepted checkpoint, or a tile is not mirrored.

get.summary: Computed inclusion proof for an ISCC-ID.

get.description: Returns a raw mirrored tlog-tiles hash tile or entry bundle BLOB at its canonical tlog-tiles path (e.g. `tile/0/000`, `tile/entries/000`), served verbatim from the local mirror.

parameters.description: The canonical tlog-tiles tile/bundle path suffix (may contain slashes).
parameters.name: tile

200.description: The raw tile or entry-bundle BLOB.

404.description: The tile or bundle is not mirrored.

get.description: Returns a JSON verdict the caller TRUSTS the monitor for: the monitor reports the hub status, the accepted checkpoint `(size, root)`, and a Merkle-verified inclusion result for the id. This is the EXPLICITLY WEAKER, NON-AUTHORITATIVE tier-1 path — "the monitor reports". The authoritative path is tier-2: fetch the proof bundle (`GET /inclusion/{iscc_id}.bundle`) and verify it yourself, removing the monitor from the trust path. An id-shaped fault (unknown id, no accepted checkpoint, leaf out of tree, tile not mirrored) is a `200 {verified:false, reason}`, never a 4xx/5xx.

parameters.description: The ISCC-ID to verify (with or without the `ISCC:` prefix).
parameters.name: iscc_id

parameters.description: An explicit committed leaf sequence to verify.
parameters.name: index

200.description: The verify-for-me verdict (verified true or false with a reason).

500.description: A genuine infrastructure fault (store read error or store inconsistency).

get.summary: verify-for-me verdict (the explicitly weaker, non-authoritative path).

servers.description: This monitor instance (relative to its own origin).
